record_notes.DCP-LETT-1432: June 7, 1851 thanks for a missing Higgins note and bank credit of 184 pounds 9 shillings 5 pence. Hopes for agricultural improvement and removal of the fifteen-percent reduction while wishing not to press Hardy. Reports own improved health and Susan poor health. Earlier 1850 outgoing letters are background, not incoming prompts; this remittance is not their earlier payment.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1483: June 19, supplied 1852. Acknowledges 183 pounds 4 shillings 11 pence; the account-book gross amount includes a separate five-pound school donation. Requests a reasoned comparison of the fifteen-percent reduction, local landowners, initial rent level, new buildings and no timber/game preservation. Darwin explicitly supports free trade but balances tenant welfare and his return; permanent adjustment is a proposal, not executed lease. Permits reply at leisure and plans forwarding to Susan. Missing remittance note is not Higgins later July answer.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1484F: July 27, 1852 survives as a copy, not the original autograph. Explicitly answers the June 19 letter after election work. Higgins argues for tenant investment and continued fifteen-percent allowance, with separate Beesby and Susan Claythorpe calculations, cattle losses, labour wages and his son farm experience. Distinguish his protectionist claims from Darwin free-trade position. MathML gives Beesby 3 1/4 percent and Claythorpe 3 1/2 percent, not 314 or 312 percent. Literal 240 quarters at 30 shillings paired with 456 pounds is arithmetically inconsistent; preserve source wording and do not silently change 30 to 38 or 456 to 360. Conclusions and historical monetary units remain source claims.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1484G: July 29, supplied 1852 based on the July 27 source. Explicitly acknowledges the long detailed case for continuing fifteen-percent allowance and accepts hoping for better times. Requests a more permanent arrangement with Hardy before long; this is not an executed lease or rent change. The full three retained blocks, including addressee line, survive. Reading of 1484F is demonstrated by July 29, physical receipt day unstated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1484H: July 31, 1852 survives as a copy. Explicitly responds to July 29 and identifies his own July 27 letter. Asks what permanent arrangement means, warns against lease or corn-rent because a possible price rise would be missed, cites managed rents and distinct old-estate versus recent-purchase reductions, and compares Erasmus, Charles and Susan holdings. Gold influx and improved prices are expectations, not known future outcomes. His claim that bad legislation caused distress is Higgins view, not Darwin agreement.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1485: August 2, supplied 1852. Answers the July 31 lease warning and the explicit gold/currency consideration. Darwin explains contrary impressions from print and a Worcestershire connection, accepts leases are unusual under Higgins care and sees a sufficient reason against a long lease. Edward Holland identity is editorial, not explicitly named by Darwin. Whole surviving three-block reply is supported; no independent physical receipt day.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1494: December 18, supplied 1852. Thanks for missing note and net remittance of 188 pounds 15 shillings 2 pence; reports modest agricultural improvement and trusts Higgins on rent. Account-book gross amount and later January 8 posting are separate evidence, not the date of the missing note or Darwin first knowledge. No new incoming letter survives here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1513: April 11, supplied 1853. Initiated instruction to record change of banker to Union Bank, Charing Cross branch. It is historical letter content, not authority to operate a bank now. No incoming prompt or Higgins completed action is identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1519: June 14, supplied 1853. Bank notice arrived this morning, separately from Higgins missing June 7 note. Acknowledges net 201 pounds 3 shillings 2 pence; five-pound school donation accounts for gross figure in ledger. Welcomes notice that next half-year should restore full rent; actual later December full payment is not June completion. Do not assign the bank notice morning receipt to Higgins letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1541: December 2–3, supplied 1853, with internal dateline. P1–2 on December 2 arrange December 10 meeting and cannot recall acknowledging an older note. P3–4 explicitly dated December 3 acknowledge a newly received Higgins note/account and separate Union Bank credit of 225 pounds 6 shillings 5 pence. P5 asks about stamped half-yearly receipts; its MathML is 1/2, not twelve-yearly, and no independent date is supplied. Preserve original range and section dates, not one earliest date for all knowledge. Later account-book gross amount and tax explanation remain apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1560: March 18, supplied 1854. Revises contemplated farm budget to at most fifteen thousand, ideally twelve to fourteen thousand, and expects Powis repayment July 1. Cash can wait while a suitable purchase is found. No farm bought and no repayment yet; later investment-book repayment confirmation is future. No answer requested is historical prose, not a restriction on research.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1561: March 23, supplied 1854. Thanks for a missing Higgins reply despite no reply intended, rejects marsh farms and welcomes the Great Northern debenture suggestion. Darwin March 18 outgoing note prompted the missing reply, not this incoming side. No investment has been reported completed here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1566: April 9, supplied 1854. Considers switching fourteen thousand pounds into guaranteed railway shares because prices have fallen, with a hypothetical nearly-five-percent return and depreciation reserve. Unnamed relative advice is distinct from Higgins advice. Asks whether a farm survey incurred costs and says he encloses five guineas for prior help; later July 8 account entry is not April settlement evidence. Farm purchase remains a fallback if railway prices rise before July. These are his historical expectations, not guaranteed realised returns.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1594: October 5, supplied 1854. A missing Higgins letter and plan offer a nearby estate, but Darwin declines because money is now invested, much for seven years. Explicitly reports following Higgins suggestion by Great Northern mortgage and B shares. This is completed-investment evidence by October 5, unlike March/April plans. Detailed July transaction dates, amounts and 4 1/4-percent rate are quoted later from the investment book; keep their source and chronology separate. No surviving covering offer or plan is identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1615: Christmas Day 1854. Acknowledges missing note/account and net credit 217 pounds 16 shillings 8 pence. Gross account figure differs by fifteen-shilling Agricultural Club payment. Wishes Higgins family well and reports two sons improving after fever and inflammation; their identities and later diary interval are editorial evidence, not all events known on Christmas. The original receipt and forthcoming calendar dates stay distinct.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1687: May 26, 1855. Short acknowledgement of half-year rent 212 pounds 6 shillings 5 pence and good farm report. The incoming report/account is unlocated. Earlier 1854 Christmas credit and July 1852 rent argument cannot substitute for this missing prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1326: Explicit prior primary reading reused with matching pins. May 9, supplied 1850. Accepts Higgins proposal of a 15 percent reduction for the past half-year, hopes depressed times temporary and compares prices under protection and in France. Asks whether Hardy works actively and has any complaint. Specific proposal is missing; 1279 is Darwin own earlier concern, not an incoming prompt. Editorial continuation of reduced income through 1852 is future knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1334: Explicit prior primary reading reused with matching pins. May 27, supplied 1850. Explicitly received Higgins letter and account this morning; separately advised by bankers of £183 5s 11d draft. Glad of good account of Hardy farming. These are two distinct communications; neither text survives. Exact morning receipt is supported for missing Higgins note, not for 1161 or all prior financial news.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1375: Explicit prior primary reading reused with matching pins. December 13, supplied 1850. Missing December 9 letter and account report £187 15s 11d draft. Regrets continued 15 percent reduction, hopes agricultural improvement and answers health inquiry. Prior outgoing 1326 establishes his agreement to reduction but is not an incoming letter. No more specific receipt date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1377: Explicit prior primary reading reused with matching pins. December 21, supplied 1850. Prospective nearly £5000 investment, asks land-market advice and moderate return; explicitly has not decided to buy. Family obligations motivate caution. Postscript cannot remember result of Mason proposed small-parcel purchase, connecting topic to 1117 without establishing any missing reply or completed sale. Expected source of funds from Emma trust is editorial inference, not body certainty. This opens an inquiry rather than answering the March 1848 note.

reading_method: Sixteen target sources independently read in full with headers, XML date constraints, excluded salutations, footnotes and bibliography. Four earlier contexts reuse explicit primary reading. Direct raw DOM inspection confirms mixed-number MathML, half-yearly fraction and the literal inconsistent wheat-price row. No figures.
